Spookling
CR ¼

As you examine the intricately designed padlock on the chest, you notice a slight shimmer. Suddenly, the “padlock” unfurls into a tiny, six-legged creature with glinting black eyes. It lets out a soft chirp before scurrying away with surprising speed.

XP 100
N Diminutive aberration (shapechanger)
Init +3; Senses darkvision 30 ft.; Perception +5

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 17, flat-footed 14 (+3 Dex, +4 size)
hp 5 (1d8+1)
Fort +1, Ref +3, Will +2

OFFENSE

Speed 15 ft., climb 15 ft.
Melee bite +5 (1d2-4), tongue +5 (special)
Space 1 ft.; Reach 0 ft.
Special Attacks sticky tongue (Diminutive or smaller only)

STATISTICS

Str 1, Dex 17, Con 12, Int 6, Wis 11, Cha 10
Base Atk +0; CMB -5, CMD 5 (13 vs. trip)
Feats Weapon Finesse
Skills Climb +11, Perception +5, Stealth +19
Languages understands Undercommon and Silent Speech (Xeniomorph)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Mimic Accessory (Ex)

As a standard action, a Spookling can assume the shape of any Diminutive or Fine object that could serve as an accessory (such as a padlock, brooch, or small ornament). This grants it a +20 racial bonus on Disguise checks to appear as that object. A Spookling using this ability can maintain its shape indefinitely and can revert to its natural form as a free action.

Sticky Tongue (Ex)

A Spookling can make a melee touch attack with its sticky tongue. On a hit against a Diminutive or smaller creature, the target is affected as though by a tanglefoot bag (Reflex DC 11 negates). The Spookling can only affect one target at a time with its tongue. The effect lasts for 2d4 rounds or until the Spookling releases the target (a free action). The save DC is Constitution-based.

Six-Legged Stability

Spooklings gain a +8 racial bonus to their CMD against trip attempts due to their six- legged stance.

ECOLOGY

Environment any (usually with Xeniomorphs)
Organization solitary, pair, or cluster (3–12)
Treasure none

Spooklings are tiny, six-legged aberrations kept as pets by Xeniomorphs. These curious creatures possess between two to five small black eyes and have the ability to shapeshift into small accessories, making them perfect companions for their shapeshifting masters. Despite their diminutive size, Spooklings retain the sharp teeth and sticky tongue characteristic of their larger kin, though their tongue is only effective against equally tiny creatures.

Spooklings are typically found in the company of Xeniomorphs, often disguised as small accessories or ornaments on their masters’ mimicked forms. They are omnivorous and can subsist on small insects, plant matter, or scraps from their Xeniomorph companions. Spooklings communicate with each other and their masters through a series of chirps, whistles, and subtle color changes in their eyes.

These tiny shapeshifters are valued by Xeniomorphs for their ability to add intricate details to their disguises, as well as for their keen senses that can alert their masters to potential dangers. In the wild, Spooklings form small clusters, working together to hunt larger prey or defend against predators.

In combat, Spooklings rely on stealth and deception. They prefer to remain hidden, using their Mimic Accessory ability to avoid detection. If forced to fight, they use their superior numbers (when in a cluster) to distract and confuse enemies. Against Diminutive or smaller threats, they employ their sticky tongues to immobilize prey before delivering a decisive bite.
